_notes: Does an EXPLICIT unintended-consequences clause fix the one thing every other arm failed at?

Evidence this exists to answer: on options-proposal, 'real-downsides' scored 0/5 with no instructions and 1/5 with the original draft — even though that draft explicitly asks for 'the pros/cons of all options'. Only the tightened rewrite's blunter phrasing reached 3-4/5. So the clause was being asked for and ignored.

draft-v2.md = the original draft VERBATIM plus 109 words: consider your own change's side effects before proposing; focus on what the user will EXPERIENCE rather than read about; the test is whether he would connect the difference back to the change, because if not he will assume it regressed.

Only ONE arm here on purpose. The other three arms' scores for options-proposal were measured on 2026-08-13 in the same fixture with the same judge, so this is compared against those rather than re-paying for them.

WATCH THE PADDING SCORE, not just real-downsides. draft-v2 is the longest arm (212 words vs 103 original, 148 tightened), and across every arm tested so far a longer instruction produced a longer answer and a WORSE padding score. If real-downsides rises while padding falls, that is a trade to decide on, not a win.
name: claude-md-guidance-v2
